cells.requirement: Referencing the connector makes it available through ordinary `AddKoan()` with no provider registration call.
An explicit provider/source resolves exactly or fails with available choices and a correction.
An available but unelected connector performs no connection, file, shape, or readiness I/O.
Two Koan hosts do not share mutable plans, readiness state, keepers, or logical client state.
Host disposal releases every host-owned provider resource.
An ordinary source with no override resolves to `StorageLifecycle: Managed` and `Access: ReadWrite`.
Every physical shape the connector claims to validate is compared by definition, not name. An incompatible same-named object is unhealthy; repair occurs only under explicit managed lifecycle policy.
External lifecycle policy performs no repair mutation or implicit provider auto-create.
Explicitly authorized provision/repair creates or reconciles the declared shape, post-validates it, and is idempotent; a repeated healthy call performs no mutation.
Every supported identity and value boundary round-trips without culture- or JSON-induced drift.
Get-many returns one slot per requested identity in input order, with `null` for each missing or invisible record.
Upsert and delete report correct outcomes for insert, update, missing, conflict, and provider-failure cases.

Each exposed delete-all, remove strategy, native bulk path, and batch operation preserves active guards, transforms, Entity lifecycle callbacks, and isolation. Each path is a separate case; optimization never widens scope or changes announced atomicity.
Deferred batch mutation loads at commit time, has a specified missing-record outcome, and participates in the same conflict and atomicity contract as other queued work.
Query results match the shared CLR oracle for each declared filter operator.
Sort, page, projection, and count receipts match work the provider actually performed; each handled component is a separate case.
Each unsupported Entity operation rejects before unbounded work or partial mutation.
A provider-bounded page/stream applies the requested bound and complete order natively, reports an accurate receipt, propagates cancellation, and releases resources on early disposal.
Each write surface fails before Entity callbacks, readiness, transaction creation, or provider I/O for that operation on a read-only source.
Each storage-lifecycle/provisioning surface fails at the same boundary on an external source.
External/read-write semantic `DeleteAll` remains legal. A clear primitive is legal only after Data proves equivalence; `Optimized` may downgrade, while explicitly structural `Fast` rejects.
Nested context, mapping, Direct/connection override, transaction, batch, instruction, and provider extension paths cannot elevate either source restriction; each exposed path is a case.
Every registered read has effective effect `Read`; `Unknown` rejects before execution.
Facts and exceptions report effective policy without exposing the connection string.
Listing is bounded, distinguishes `Complete`, `MoreAvailable`, and `ProviderLimit`, and returns a source-bound opaque continuation exactly when the provider can resume.
Resolution uses provider-safe identifier handling, returns a source-bound opaque reference, reports typed ambiguity and safe candidates, and rejects a reference used with the wrong source.
Description is non-mutating and reports honest provider kind, intrinsic traits, source-policy-projected effective operations, optional neutral shape, and diagnostic-only display path.
Sampling is available only for intrinsic `Records` and effective `Sample`, is bounded, uses the regular shared shape or one nested document value, reports completion, and never mutates.
Field order, duplicate names, provider type, missing, null, binary, temporal, numeric, JSON, and nested values survive neutral materialization.
Ambiguous name lookup rejects, ordinal lookup remains lossless, and an additional result channel rejects rather than being discarded.

DTO projection uses a reused ordinal plan for immutable constructor/positional-record and writable-property binding, with corrective missing/duplicate/type failures and no dictionary-to-JSON conversion.

Every buffered result has positive record/value/aggregate/duration limits, uses the shared byte-accounting basis, omits rather than clips the first non-fitting record, and reports the first honest completion reason; cancellation, timeout, conversion, and provider failure remain failures.
Provider-native inspection preserves richer metadata in an explicit provider type and neither widens nor mislabels the neutral descriptor or `RecordSet` contract.
An identity-plus-object mapping round-trips.
Flat scalar names, including nested logical property paths, round-trip.
Hybrid authoritative scalar bindings and structured subtrees round-trip without duplication drift.
A flat logical scalar mapped inside a physical structured value round-trips in both directions.

Logical/physical duplicates, ambiguous paths, missing required bindings, incompatible types, and undeclared asymmetry fail plan compilation with a correction; explicit generated/read-only bindings remain legal.
Single, generated, and composite identities use every declared component consistently; a partial or nullable composite identity rejects before execution.
Each declared legacy codec is symmetric, and query/write parameters use the same physical encoding as hydration.
Read projection fetches only physical values required by the compiled map when that optimization is announced.
External read/write mapping never causes DDL.
Mapping plans are immutable, host-scoped, bounded, and reused on the warm path.

Every exposed consumer—hydration, writes, filters, ordering, patches, conditional writes, projections, and index expressions—uses the same compiled physical binding for each logical path. Each exposed consumer is a case; index-expression cases exist only with that separate profile.
A stored projection used by a query or index is maintained by every mutation case; otherwise the index derives from the canonical stored value. Fallback cannot conceal an inert index or false claim.
A declared usable index covers the same provider expression and scalar encoding emitted for its filter/order. Native plan evidence proves representative single and composite cases.
An announced rewrite-free derived/expression index benefits records already stored without rewrite. Required backfill is an explicit deployment operation and that capability remains unannounced.
TTL metadata is lowered only when native expiry semantics are announced and proved; it never becomes a meaningless ordinary index.
Duplicate `(source, name)` declarations fail composition; the catalog cannot mutate afterward.
`Query` resolves only `Read + Records + Buffered` and `Scalar<T>` only `Read + Scalar + Buffered`; result, delivery, or effect mismatch fails before provider execution.
Missing, extra, null-for-required, and incompatible parameters fail before provider execution.
The adapter receives the selected binding, frozen execution lane, reused parameter plan, effective-read decision, timeout, and bounds without reparsing application configuration.

Detectable mutation under a read declaration fails composition. Every opaque read is bound permanently to provider-enforced read-only execution; inability to establish it fails composition/validation.
`Unknown` never runs through `Query` or `Scalar` on any source.
A record result satisfies Record Results. A scalar is exactly one provider scalar or one record × one field, respects the shared value/duration bounds, and rejects every other cardinality.
External registration may carry inline payload but never provisions a provider-managed artifact.
A missing referenced provider-managed artifact fails diagnostically and is not created externally.
Registered operations are uncached, are not automatically exposed through REST/MCP, and fail closed under active segmentation unless an explicit host/control-plane scope exists.
No registered operation is replayed after provider dispatch. Bounded transient acquisition retry is pre-dispatch; provider-transparent retry must be announced and proved as its own case.
Telemetry records source, stable name, provider, effect, result kind, duration, attempts, and result count—not payload text or parameter values.
Concurrent first legitimate shape use has one readiness/provisioning outcome and no partial race.
Route readiness and shape provisioning use distinct host-scoped single-flight state. Caller cancellation detaches one wait; shutdown owns shared cancellation; failure is never cached healthy.
Pool saturation does not leak source, transaction, read-only, tenant, or provider session state to the next operation.

Caller cancellation and provider timeout remain distinct on each native operation; cancellation reaches provider dispatch and releases active request, result/cursor/stream, and transactional resources.
A claimed atomic batch leaves state wholly before/after. Pre-commit failure rolls back with a bounded independent cleanup token; an indeterminate commit reports outcome unknown and is never replayed.
Conditional replace is one native compare-and-set and reports a lost race without overwriting the winner.
Restart proves announced durability; an in-memory shim cannot pass.
The standard bounded soak leaves client/pool, handle, result/cursor/stream, task, cache, and memory counts stable.
Each announced isolation token passes the shared adversarial cross-scope cell.
`Describe` is side-effect-free and matches compiled route, policy, mappings, and capabilities.
`Explain` reports provider work, client work, bounds, and unsupported semantics before execution.
`Doctor` performs only documented non-mutating checks and gives a correction for every failure.
Startup, facts, health, errors, and tests project the same decision identities.
General facts/logs exclude credentials, parameters, business values, tenant identifiers, and full raw provider errors; safe public exceptions and restricted native evidence stay separate.

Native failures use exact provider code/type and target, never message text. Timeout is not caller cancellation; `OperationCanceledException` survives only when non-commit is known. Retryability and replay safety remain separate, and a failed mutation/existence probe never becomes success/not-found.
Warm source routing performs no DI enumeration, adapter election, policy recomputation, readiness I/O, or structural plan compilation.
Warm Entity/mapping/record paths perform no repeated reflection, mapping conflict detection, dictionary-to-JSON materialization, equivalent lookup reconstruction, or repeated physical-JSON parsing.
Route, readiness, mapping, native-operation, and operation caches are host-scoped, bounded, and invalidated by stable structural/credential rules.
No handled/optimized claim conceals a full-source materialization, client page, inert index, temporary sort, N+1 provider-dispatch loop, or other weaker execution.

Every applicable §7 benchmark records allocation, provider dispatch count, elapsed time, and provider work against a pinned baseline; structural warm-path regression or unexplained material regression fails.

The one-page responsibility map has one owner for each policy, route, readiness, mapping, materializer, and provider-execution concern; duplicate adapter-local framework machinery fails placement review.
A vector-space plan binds source, safe physical name, dimensions, metric, visibility, optional model identity, and optional named space once; an unelected provider performs no I/O.
Empty, non-finite, wrong-dimension, or wrong-space embeddings reject before mutation; every valid boundary value round-trips without drift.
Saving a new identity inserts one point; saving it again atomically replaces embedding and metadata without a duplicate.
Delete returns the correct existing/missing outcome; provider failure never reports success and does not widen scope.
Get-one returns one complete point or `null`; get-many preserves input count, order, and duplicates, with `null` in every missing slot.
Metadata survives the neutral value algebra without reserved-field collision, shape invention, provider objects, or missing/null confusion.
Search returns at most `Top`, no duplicate identity, descending similarity, and stable identity tie order; empty and fewer-than-requested results are normal.
Similarity is finite `[0,1]`, higher is closer, monotonic for the declared metric, and `AtLeast` is applied equivalently or rejected before unbounded work.
Search uses exactly the declared source, dimensions, metric, model, and named space; a point or query from another space never mixes silently.
Exact/Approximate and candidate facts report provider work honestly; approximation is never presented as an exact oracle result.
Default Session visibility makes each awaited save/delete observable to subsequent get and search operations in the same source without arbitrary sleeps.
Explicit Eventual visibility may defer search visibility; `Sync` is cancellable, bounded, and makes every earlier accepted mutation in that source visible or fails.
`Where` constrains the candidate set before ranking. The shared filter oracle agrees for every announced operator; residual or post-filter fallback rejects before provider I/O or unbounded work.
Hybrid search defines `SemanticWeight` endpoints as pure lexical/vector modes, preserves normalized final rank, and rejects unsupported text/weight combinations before I/O.
Each named space keeps immutable dimensions, metric, and model; unsupported or ambiguous selection fails with safe available choices.
A continuation is opaque and bound to source, space, query, filter, and ordering; resume has no duplicates or gaps inside its declared snapshot contract, and wrong-context reuse rejects.
Native bulk save/delete preserves per-item outcomes, cancellation, guards, visibility, and isolation; dispatch count and partial failure are reported honestly.
An Atomic Batch claim is all-or-nothing under injected mid-batch failure; otherwise the result is explicitly non-atomic and retains every item outcome.
Export is provider-bounded, cancellable, and yields every visible point exactly once under its stated snapshot or weak-consistency contract without materializing the corpus.

Ensure, validate, and clear obey lifecycle and access policy, compare the complete space shape, never auto-create under External, and keep visibility synchronization distinct from destructive clearing.

Every announced vector isolation mode prevents cross-scope get, search, export, and delete and maps to the declared metadata or physical-address mechanism; a pinned conflicting name rejects at plan time.
Entity/vector coordination never invents cross-store atomicity; every injected stage failure exposes safe commit facts, retry disposition, and compensation guidance without provider secrets.
Cancellation, timeout, rate limit, schema mismatch, unavailable provider, and disposal map to the shared failure taxonomy; disposal releases clients, cursors, polling, and background work.

Warm single save/get/search, native bulk, filtered search, and materialization meet pinned provider-relative budgets with one compiled immutable plan and no per-result reflection or metadata-shape rebuild.

profiles.applicability: any mapping, projection, index, or other expected physical shape is declared
connector may provision or repair physical shape
connector can create/alter/drop or may implicitly create storage
Entity Persistence exposes semantic data writes under `External + ReadWrite`
provider samples a declared record-producing container
neutral buffered records are returned by any surface
one identity value and one complete structured value are claimed
scalar physical names, including nested logical paths, are claimed
scalar values and a structured subtree are claimed together
a flat property binds inside a physical structured value
existing records are announced to benefit without rewrite
an all-or-nothing batch token is announced
richer native metadata extension is exposed
more than one vector space per point is announced
native bulk save or delete is announced
